cards.subject: The sermon at a Sunday Mass, seen from across the nave at the height of a tall carved wooden pulpit fixed to a stone pillar, with a carved sounding board above it. In the pulpit, the priest, having laid aside his chasuble and maniple, stands in amice, lace alb and a white-and-gold stole crossed over his breast, in profile, and preaches, one hand resting on the pulpit's rail and the other open toward the people, his face earnest and kind. Below him the congregation sits in the wooden pews, small, faces turned up to listen: a mother in a lace veil with a sleeping baby, an old farmer, schoolchildren in a row. Far off, beyond the altar rail, the high altar with its gradine, crucifix, tall lit candles and white-veiled tabernacle, and his chasuble laid over the seat of the sedilia. Late-morning light slants across the pillars. Attentive, warm. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.

cards.subject: The Offertory at a Sunday Mass, seen close from the side of the high altar, in profile. The priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, stands at the middle of the altar facing it and holds the golden paten with the large white host raised to the height of his breast with both hands, his eyes lifted to the crucifix; before him lies the unfolded white corporal, and beside it the golden chalice, its veil laid aside, with a folded white purificator. The Missal rests on its stand, its pages showing no letters, and the centre altar card leans against the white-veiled tabernacle; the tall lit candles rise on the gradine. At the epistle corner a server in cassock and surplice waits on the step with the glass cruets of wine and water on their small dish. Beyond the altar rail, soft and far, the congregation kneels and sits in the pews. Warm candlelight, quiet offering. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: The corporal, purificator, chalice and Missal are placed on the altar and the faithful bring up the bread and wine (GIRM 73, 139–140); the priest 'holds it slightly raised above the altar with both hands and says quietly' the blessing of the excerpt, then the minister presents the cruets (GIRM 141–142; the Order of Mass rubric). The people sit (GIRM 43). 'Slightly raised', not the elevation: the paten stays just above the altar.

cards.subject: The Sanctus at a Sunday sung Mass, seen from the choir stalls at the side of the sanctuary, close to the altar. The priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, stands at the middle of the high altar facing it, in profile, bowing moderately with his hands joined; on the step a server in cassock and surplice kneels and rings a small bell, and four torchbearers in cassock and surplice enter with tall lit torches. Behind and above the altar, beyond its gradine with six tall lit candles and the white-veiled tabernacle, rises a tall gilded reredos painted on a gold ground with rows of angels and six-winged red seraphim, all turned in adoration toward its centre, where a carved crucifix stands. cards.subject: The Hanc igitur and Quam oblationem, the moment just before the Consecration, seen close from just behind and to the right of the priest, looking over his shoulder down onto the altar. The priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, stands at the middle of the high altar facing it, his two hands spread together, palms down, over the offerings: on the white corporal, the large white Host lying directly on the linen, and behind it the golden chalice covered with its stiff white pall. The Missal on its stand beside them and the centre altar card leaning against the white-veiled tabernacle, their pages showing no letters; the crucifix and tall lit candles rise on the gradine beyond. High above the altar, in a round stained-glass window, the Holy Spirit as a white dove in golden rays, and a soft light falls from it onto the gifts. On the edge of the foot-pace below, a server in cassock and surplice kneels and rings a small bell in warning. The faithful kneel beyond the altar rail, unseen but for a hush. Still, expectant, luminous. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.

A little before the Consecration a minister may ring a small bell (GIRM 150); the faithful kneel after the Sanctus (GIRM 43, USCCB). The dove is glass in the church's window.

cards.subject: The Consecration at a sung Mass, seen straight on from the foot of the altar steps, the altar the centre. At a white-and-gold high altar with gradines, six tall lit candles, a crucifix, the three altar cards and the tabernacle veiled in white, the priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, seen from behind, facing the altar, raises the white Host high above his head with both hands. Behind him, kneeling on the edge of the foot-pace, a server in cassock and white lace surplice lifts the hem of the chasuble with one hand; on the step at the right a second server kneels and rings a small bell; at the epistle side a kneeling thurifer swings a smoking thurible toward the Host; four torchbearers kneel in a line across the sanctuary floor, holding tall lit torches. Soft golden rays fall from above onto the Host. At the very bottom of the arch, the heads and shoulders of the faithful kneeling at the altar rail, seen from behind, the women veiled. Figures small in the scene. Adoring, still. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: After the words over the bread the priest 'shows the consecrated host to the people, places it again on the paten, and genuflects in adoration' (the Order of Mass rubric, Eucharistic Prayer II; GIRM 79d); a minister rings the small bell at each elevation according to local custom, and if incense is used a minister incenses the host when it is shown (GIRM 150). The faithful kneel (GIRM 43, USCCB). Composed as the x_consecration test draft (2026-09-29), without its server lifting the chasuble's hem, which the rubrics don't give.
